metadata.title: TLCTC Mapping — Mandiant M-Trends 2026 MITRE ATT&CK Appendix
metadata.description: Maps MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed by Mandiant during 2025 incident response (M-Trends 2026 report, pp. 85-101) to TLCTC v2.0 threat clusters. Each technique entry records the observed percentage of investigations, the TLCTC cluster(s) it maps to, and rationale grounded in the framework's classification rules (R-ROLE, R-EXEC, R-CRED, Axiom III, Axiom X). Cluster assignments are cross-referenced against the canonical enterprise mapping (mappings/mitre-attack-enterprise/tlctc-enterprise-attack.json).
metadata.source: Mandiant M-Trends 2026 report, MITRE ATT&CK Appendix (pp. 85-101)
metadata.source_sample: 500k+ hours of Mandiant frontline incident-response investigations in 2025

notation.arrow: A → B means A enables or leads to B (attack sequence)
notation.pipe: A | B means either A or B depending on context
notation.parens: Parentheses group multi-step paths within alternatives
notation.na: N/A means the technique is attacker-side preparation not observable on victim systems (reconnaissance, resource development)

classification_axioms_applied.axiom_iii: Threats are causes, not outcomes. Ransomware (T1486) classifies by cause (FEC execution = #7) not by outcome.
classification_axioms_applied.axiom_x_r_cred: Credential acquisition maps to the enabling cluster; credential USE (T1078, T1021, T1550, T1558) is ALWAYS #4.
classification_axioms_applied.r_role: Exploitation is classified by the role of the flawed component: server-role = #2, client-role = #3.
classification_axioms_applied.r_exec: Every FEC execution must record a #7 step.
classification_axioms_applied.r_supply: #10 is placed at the Trust Acceptance Event.

phases.note: Reconnaissance and Resource Development tactics. These techniques are attacker-side activities (scanning, capability staging) not directly observable on the victim network. TLCTC classifies what happens TO the defender; purely attacker-side preparation maps to N/A. Where reconnaissance touches victim assets via legitimate exposed functions (e.g., DNS queries, public website scraping), it is #1 Abuse of Functions.

techniques.rationale: Passive gathering is N/A; where querying exposed enterprise services, #1.
DNS queries against victim's authoritative servers are a designed-as-intended function, abused for recon.
Social-engineering lure targeting the human; no FEC required, just information elicitation.
Probing exposed enterprise services via their designed protocols — legitimate function, abused scope.
Same as parent — abused use of exposed service responses.
Deceives victim into visiting attacker-controlled content — social-engineering vector.
Attacker acquisition; the downstream USE of the signed binary on victim appears under #7/masquerading.
Attacker use of LLMs for capability development.

If the compromised infrastructure is a third-party system that the attacker then uses to attack downstream targets, the initial compromise maps per R-ROLE (#2/#3); downstream trust honoring maps to #10 at the TAE.

phases.note: Initial Access + Credential Access (acquisition). R-ROLE dictates exploitation classification: public-facing apps are server-role (#2), client-side vulnerabilities are #3. Valid Accounts and supply-chain trust honoring are separate clusters (#4, #10). Credential acquisition maps to enabling cluster; credential USE is always #4.

techniques.rationale: R-ROLE: exploited component is in server role → #2 Exploiting Server. Top 2025 vector.

Use of VPN / RDP / remote services typically requires authentication; R-CRED: credential application is always #4. If used without creds via an exploit, the exploit step is #2 and this is the post-exploit artifact.
Axiom X / R-CRED: credential application is ALWAYS #4, regardless of how the credential was acquired.
Targets human psychological susceptibility → #9 Social Engineering. If the lure delivers FEC that executes, add a downstream #7.
Voice-channel social engineering. M-Trends 2026: vishing is the #2 initial-access vector in 2025 (UNC6040).
Social engineering over third-party messaging platform.
Lure is #9; if the attachment's FEC executes, it is a separate #7 step.
R-ROLE: exploits a flaw in the victim's client (browser) → #3 Exploiting Client.
R-SUPPLY: #10 at the Trust Acceptance Event where the compromised upstream artifact becomes authoritative in the target domain.
TAE at install/update of the compromised software.
Physical attack — attacker-supplied hardware placed on the target network.
FEC via USB executes → #7; physical insertion of unauthorized media is #8.
TAE: the target honors a trust artifact from a compromised third party.
Attacker interposes on the path and injects content (#5 MitM); the injected content then lands in the victim's browser as social engineering (#9), client-side exploit (#3), or FEC (#7).
Reading credential stores via legitimate OS functions (SAM, NTDS.dit, LSASS handles) is #1. If a foreign tool (Mimikatz, GoSecretsDump) is introduced and executes, add #7 for the FEC step.
Reading the AD database via legitimate file/volume access.
Process memory read via legitimate API = #1; if Mimikatz/ProcDump introduced = #7.
Abuse of legitimate AD replication protocol — #1 par excellence.
Registry/LSA read via legitimate OS function.
Reading credentials from files/registry/metadata via legitimate access.
IMDS is a designed endpoint; querying it from a compromised workload is scope abuse.
Reading browser/password-manager DBs via legitimate file access.
Key Vault / Secrets Manager API abuse.
Infostealer reads browser DB via legitimate access (orchestrated by #7 implant if applicable).
AiTM interception of OTP/session = #5 MitM; if intercept is via malicious browser extension or on-host agent reading tokens, it shifts toward #1/#7.
Guessing credentials to authenticate → credential application path → #4.
Modifying auth flow via legitimate config (Skeleton Key-less variants) is #1; installing a malicious auth DLL/module is #7.
Disabling/modifying MFA policy via legitimate admin action.
Installing a malicious PAM module = FEC.
Foreign DLL loaded into LSA = FEC.
Forging/harvesting tickets is credential-material acquisition (#1); using the ticket to authenticate is #4 (Axiom X).
Legitimate Kerberos SPN request → offline crack; ticket request is #1, subsequent auth is separately #4.
Forge TGT with KRBTGT hash (#1); use of ticket is #4.
Passive capture on-wire = #5; promiscuous read on compromised host's own NIC can be #1 if designed function.
Coercing auth to attacker-controlled endpoint then capturing hash.
OAuth consent phishing = #9; direct token theft from a compromised store = #1.
ADCS ESC1/ESC8 certificate issuance abuse = #1; use of cert to authenticate is #4.

phases.note: Execution + Persistence. R-EXEC: every foreign-executable-content execution is #7. Persistence via legitimate OS mechanisms (scheduled tasks, registry run keys) is #1 when the orchestration is legit-function abuse; where a foreign binary is dropped/registered, the registration is #1 but the subsequent FEC execution is #7.

techniques.rationale: Shell/interpreter running attacker-supplied script = FEC execution. LotL invocation of powershell.exe with malicious script: #1 launches a legitimate interpreter, which then executes the foreign script = #7. Top-observed technique (45.9%).
ESXi shell commands via legitimate admin path = #1; attacker-supplied script = #7.
Legitimate cloud API calls from compromised identity.
Victim is socially engineered (#9) into running attacker content; execution is #7.
Link click lands on payload page; browser-side exploit = #3, downloaded binary execution = #7.
ClickFix / fake-CAPTCHA pattern — M-Trends highlights this as a 2025 trend.
Service-manager abuse to execute commands. PsExec / svcctl call is #1; the payload started as the service is #7 if it's a foreign binary.
PsExec-style remote service creation → executes foreign binary.
schtasks/at creation is #1 (designed function); if the task runs a foreign binary, execution is a separate #7.
WMI is a designed remote-execution surface — #1; payload launched is #7 if foreign.
DCOM/COM abuse for execution — depends on foreign content.
Legitimate cloud admin commands from compromised principal.
kubectl exec / docker exec — legit admin plane abuse.
Deploying attacker-controlled container image = TAE-adjacent; execution inside is #7.
Maintaining remote-service access via valid credentials = #4.
Adding keys/groups/roles via legitimate IAM APIs — designed function, abused scope.
Adding SP secret / access key via legitimate API.
Service creation via legit API; if the service runs a foreign binary, #7.
sc.exe creates service → foreign binary runs.
Installing web shell / foreign server module = FEC.
Web shell is FEC hosted by the compromised server. Note: observation percentage exceeds parent due to reporting methodology.
Run-key / startup registration is #1; the payload started is #7 if foreign.
Registry value set → foreign binary runs at logon.
Foreign SSP DLL loaded by LSA = FEC.
Search-order / permissions abuse places foreign DLL into legitimate load path; resulting load is FEC.
Registry ACL abuse redirects service binary.

techniques.techniqueName: Path Interception by Search Order Hijacking

techniques.rationale: WMI subscriptions / COM hijack trigger FEC.
Legitimate WMI subscription API abuse → foreign script runs.
OAuth app / integration registration — designed extensibility, abused scope.
Installing malicious browser/app extension = FEC package.
Foreign extension executes in browser context.
Legitimate rule creation abused for forwarding / persistence (no FEC).
Trojanized legit binary = foreign code masquerading.

phases.note: Credential Access (dumping for higher-privilege creds) + Privilege Escalation. Credential acquisition is #1; its subsequent use for higher privilege is #4. Process Injection and Exploitation for PrivEsc are #7 and #2 respectively.

techniques.rationale: Group membership add via designed IAM API.
Injecting foreign code into a legitimate process = FEC running under that process's identity.
R-ROLE: the exploited component (kernel driver, service) is in server role relative to the attacker-process → #2.
UAC/sudo abuse via legitimate elevation API.
UAC bypass via designed auto-elevation paths.
Impersonate/duplicate token via designed Win32 API → authenticate as another user. Token-use end-state is effectively #4.
GPO/tenant policy change via designed IAM.

phases.note: Discovery tactic. All legitimate OS/cloud query APIs abused for enumeration. Uniformly #1 Abuse of Functions — no FEC, no exploit, no credential acquisition. The implant or session orchestrating the queries may itself be classified separately, but each discovery call is designed-as-intended.

techniques.rationale: Legitimate FS APIs abused for enumeration. Top-observed discovery technique.

phases.note: Execution (re-used from Foothold) + Lateral Movement tactic. Remote service use with valid credentials is #4 (R-CRED / Axiom X). Pass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Ticket / App Access Token use are all #4. Lateral Tool Transfer is #7 (delivering foreign binary to next hop).

techniques.rationale: Remote service authentication with valid credentials → #4. Top-observed lateral technique.
Axiom X: use of any credential material is #4.
Transferring foreign binary to next hop → downstream FEC.
Poisoned file on share — next user opens it (#9) and FEC runs (#7).

phases.note: Defense Evasion + Persistence (re-observed) + Command and Control. Masquerading and obfuscation of foreign code are #7. Legitimate-function abuse for hiding/disabling is #1. C2 via attacker-controlled infrastructure is #7 (the C2 channel itself is FEC behavior); C2 via legitimate cloud services (T1102) is #1 (LotX pattern).

techniques.rationale: Obfuscation is a property of the foreign code → still #7 at execution.
Deleting logs/files via legitimate OS APIs.

techniques.techniqueName: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs

techniques.rationale: Legitimate admin APIs abused to disable logging/tooling.

techniques.techniqueName: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System

techniques.rationale: Decoding step occurs inside FEC runtime.
LOLBAS binary invoked (#1) to run foreign script (#7).
Foreign code disguised as legit — still #7.

techniques.techniqueName: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

techniques.rationale: Renamed LOLBAS used as foreign tool.
Modifying OS trust store via designed API — abused scope.

techniques.techniqueName: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions

techniques.rationale: forfiles/pcalua abuse to proxy foreign command.
Raw disk read via legit API.
Human impersonation (CEO fraud / helpdesk vish) → #9 Social Engineering.
Cloud admin API abuse to stop/modify VMs.
DCShadow-style: attacker-controlled DC registered; foreign component introduced into replication topology.
Remote template loaded into Office doc = FEC fetch.
Router NAT/ACL abuse via legitimate admin plane.
Fetching foreign tool onto host is FEC-delivery precondition → #7 at subsequent execution.
C2 hosted on legitimate cloud service (Google Calendar, Dropbox, etc.) — LotX pattern, legit function abused.
Legit SaaS API for two-way C2.
C2 over HTTP(S)/DNS/SMTP from attacker infrastructure — the C2 traffic is attacker-supplied.
Attacker proxy = #7; abusing legit corp proxy = #1.
Legitimate tool (AnyDesk, ScreenConnect) installed by attacker — installation is #7 (foreign binary) but subsequent use of its designed remote-access function is #1.
Physical rogue device providing remote access.

phases.note: Collection + Exfiltration + Impact. Collection and exfiltration via legitimate APIs are #1 (the orchestrating implant/session may be classified separately). Encrypted-for-impact ransomware is #7 at the encryption execution — Axiom III: classify by cause, not outcome. Resource hijacking (cryptomining) is #7.

techniques.rationale: Outbound transfer via existing C2 (C2 channel classified separately as #7).
Exfil to legit cloud storage/code/text service.
File copy (#1); physical removal of media (#8).
Axiom III: 'ransomware' is an outcome label; the cause is FEC execution of the encryptor binary. DRE:Ac (data present but inaccessible). Top-observed Impact technique in 2025.
Legit service-stop API to kill backup/DB/AV before encryption.
BEC / wire-fraud flow: social engineering initiates (#9); the fraudulent transaction executes through legitimate banking/ERP functions (#1). Outcome-labeled technique — classify by cause.
vssadmin delete shadows; designed command abused. Recovery-denial cornerstone per M-Trends 2026.
Legit delete API (#1); custom wiper = #7. DRE:Av.
Cryptomining binary on victim compute = FEC. Outcome is resource consumption, cause is FEC (Axiom III).
Legit content replacement via CMS (#1); custom defacement binary (#7). DRE:I.
Legit account-disable / password-reset APIs abused to lock defenders out.

cluster_frequency_observation.note: Approximate cluster frequencies across the Mandiant 2025 corpus, derived from mapping the observed-technique percentages. Same-technique occurrences across phases are counted once per unique phase observation.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_1_dominance: #1 Abuse of Functions is the dominant TLCTC cluster across the 2025 corpus. It appears in every phase and is the sole mapping for the entire Internal Reconnaissance phase and most of Collection/Exfiltration. Reflects the 2025 shift toward living-off-the-land tradecraft.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_4_top_entry: #4 Identity Theft dominates Initial Compromise (T1133 23.8% + T1078 17.0%) and Lateral Movement (T1021 30.6%). Axiom X / R-CRED: credential use is always #4, regardless of how the credential was acquired.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_7_execution: #7 Malware appears at every FEC execution and dominates Establish Foothold (T1059 45.9%) and Maintain Presence C2 (T1105 24.5%, T1071 10.9%). Ransomware impact (T1486 17.7%) is #7 by Axiom III.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_2_exploitation: #2 Exploiting Server is the top 2025 initial-access vector (T1190 27.7%). M-Trends 2026: 6th consecutive year as #1.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_9_vishing: #9 Social Engineering driven by vishing (T1566.004 6.1%) is the #2 initial-access vector in 2025 (UNC6040).
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_3_client: #3 Exploiting Client appears primarily as drive-by compromise (T1189 6.3%) and T1203.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_10_supply_chain: #10 Supply Chain observations include T1195 (1.7%) and T1199 Trusted Relationship (0.5%) — placed at the TAE per R-SUPPLY.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_5_mitm: #5 Man-in-the-Middle is rare but structurally important: T1111 MFA interception (4.9%), T1557/T1040 sniffing, T1659 content injection.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_6_flooding: #6 Flooding Attack does not appear in the appendix — Mandiant's IR corpus is focused on targeted intrusion, not availability-only attacks.
cluster_frequency_observation.cluster_8_physical: #8 Physical Attack observations limited to T1200 (1.0%), T1091 (0.5%), T1219.003 (0.5%), T1052 (0.2%).

framework_rules_validated: Axiom III applied to T1486 (ransomware → #7 at cause, not outcome), T1496 (cryptojacking), T1657 (financial theft).
Axiom X / R-CRED applied across T1078, T1021 family, T1550 family, T1558 family — credential USE is ALWAYS #4 regardless of acquisition method.
R-EXEC applied: every FEC-delivery technique (T1059, T1105, T1204, T1543, T1505.003) produces a #7 step.
R-ROLE applied: T1190 → #2 (server-role), T1189/T1203 → #3 (client-role), T1068 → #2 (kernel/service server-role).
R-SUPPLY applied: T1195, T1195.002, T1195.003, T1199 → #10 at the TAE.
